summary: Comprehensive backend testing of the new JWT + RBAC layer for Oyun Loncası. Created /app/backend/tests/test_auth.py covering login, /auth/me, change-password, /users CRUD, JWT structure/expiry, admin seed, and RBAC on all write endpoints (members, events, points, scores, commanders, events/archive-group, seed). Also updated /app/backend/tests/backend_test.py so the shared session fixture authenticates as admin (write endpoints now require auth). All 30 auth/RBAC tests pass (100%). Overall 60/62 tests pass. The 2 failures are pre-existing seed-data drift assertions in iteration_1 tests (member rank distribution & svs group count) — NOT related to this iteration and NOT auth-caused.

minor.issue: seed_admin does NOT re-sync password if ADMIN_PASSWORD env changes after first seed. If the admin later changes their password via /auth/change-password, that is expected; but if ops rotates ADMIN_PASSWORD in .env, existing admin's hash won't be updated. Playbook recommendation was to sync on startup.
Endpoint allows an admin to demote themselves to role='user' (no self-role guard). Combined with self-delete prevention, the system could end up with zero admins.
No brute-force lockout after N failed logins (playbook mentioned lockout after 5 fails). Currently unlimited attempts allowed.

No httpOnly cookie is set - token is only returned in JSON body (matches spec: localStorage). Playbook guidance about httpOnly cookies is not applied here; acceptable since spec explicitly asks for localStorage-based JWT.

action_items: OPTIONAL: consider adding brute-force lockout on /api/auth/login (5 failures → temp block) per auth playbook.
OPTIONAL: seed_admin should also re-hash password when ADMIN_PASSWORD env changes (currently only syncs role/can_edit/email).
OPTIONAL: prevent an admin from demoting themselves in PATCH /api/users/{id} to avoid zero-admin state.

Iteration_1 tests test_members_list_156_and_rank_distribution and test_event_groups fail because current DB seed does not match iteration_1's expected 156-member GOW/R5/... distribution — DB appears to have been seeded differently (94/1/8/20/18/15 not present). If seed correctness matters, main agent may want to POST /api/seed?force=true (with admin auth) to restore the expected dataset. Not an auth bug.
critical_code_review_comments: auth.py public_user() always coerces can_edit=True for role=='admin' — good, consistent.

make_auth_deps() re-creates deps inside make_auth_router() as well; the router-scoped deps are separate closures from server.py's deps. Both hit the same db so behaviour is identical, but there is duplication.

server.py startup calls seed_data(force=False) directly, passing the Depends sentinel as `_` — this only works because require_admin is not evaluated. Fragile but currently correct; a comment already documents this.
No password_hash leakage in /api/users response (verified in test).
JWT exp is set to ~7 days (verified 6d20h < delta < 7d4h). HS256 with 64-char secret from env — good.
seed_admin uses bcrypt (verified $2b$ prefix implicitly via successful verify_password). Idempotent on subsequent startups.
updated_files: /app/backend/tests/backend_test.py (added admin_token session fixture; write endpoints now authenticated)
seed_data_creation: Test users created per-test via /api/users (prefixed test_viewer_ / test_editor_ / test_dup_ / test_todel_) and all deleted via fixture teardown / explicit cleanup. No permanent seed data added.
context_for_next_testing_agent: Auth layer is fully working. Admin seed on startup is idempotent. If iteration_1 seed-data assertions still fail (156 members, 14 events), it's because the DB doesn't match — main agent can call POST /api/seed?force=true with admin token. Test file pattern for creating auth'd users: POST /api/users with admin bearer, then POST /api/auth/login to get their token. Cleanup via DELETE /api/users/{id}. pyjwt package was installed to craft expired token in tests.
